The digital texts are OpenITI's, published under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (attribution, non-commercial, share-alike), with the editorial matter of in-copyright printed editions removed by OpenITI; seated under the same licence. normalization: None. Each text is seated as OpenITI publishes it at the pinned commit: OpenITI mARkdown (the #META# header naming the printed edition, ### headings for kitab and bab, ~~ for wrapped lines, ms/PageV page markers), in UTF-8, most texts without full vocalization. The file is its own text layer, so no second copy is emitted; each file's OpenITI version record (.yml) is seated beside it. Every file is verified against its git blob id at the pinned commit.
scope: The nine books Sunni scholarship calls al-Kutub al-Tis'a: the Muwatta of Malik, the Musnad of Ahmad ibn Hanbal, the Sunan of al-Darimi, the two Sahihs of al-Bukhari and Muslim, and the Sunans of Ibn Majah, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i (al-Mujtaba); the four books of the Imami Shi'i tradition, al-Kutub al-Arba'a: al-Kulayni's al-Kafi, Ibn Babawayh's Man la yahduruhu al-faqih, and al-Tusi's Tahdhib al-ahkam and al-Istibsar; and al-Nawawi's Forty, the most read short collection. One version of each, the version OpenITI marks PRIMARY_VERSION in its metadata. Al-Nasa'i's al-Sunan al-Kubra, Ibn Khuzayma, Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim's Mustadrak, al-Bayhaqi, the Zaydi Musnad of Zayd ibn Ali, and the Ibadi Musnad of al-Rabi' ibn Habib are in OpenITI and not seated in this pass: QUEUED. Translations are not seated.
verified_loci: Muwatta, the hadith of the two things left behind — 'تركت فيكم أمرين'
Musnad, the first musnad — 'مسند أبي بكر الصديق'
Darimi, the opening bab — 'باب ما كان عليه الناس قبل مبعث النبي'
Bukhari, hadith 1, on intentions — 'إنما الأعمال بالنيات'
Bukhari, the lawful and the unlawful — 'الحلال بين والحرام بين'
Muslim, the hadith of Jibril — 'أخبرني عن الإسلام'
Ibn Majah, seeking knowledge — 'فريضة على كل مسلم'
Abu Dawud, the renewer of each century — 'يجدد لها دينها'
Tirmidhi, the first bab — 'باب ما جاء لا تقبل صلاة بغير طهور'
al-Kafi, the opening book — 'كتاب العقل والجهل'
al-Faqih, its title in the text — 'من لا يحضره الفقيه'
Tahdhib, the first bab — 'باب الاحداث الموجبة للطهارة'
Istibsar, the measure of the kurr — 'باب كمية الكر'
why_seated: Asked for as the hadith supplementary to the Qur'an, which the shelf has held since EA-CORPORA-02/08 (the Tanzil Uthmani text): the reports of what the Prophet said and did, transmitted by chains of named reporters, which with the Qur'an make up the sources of Islamic law and practice. Both the Sunni and the Imami Shi'i canons are seated, each as its own tradition defines it.
spine: The Hadith — al-Kutub al-Tis'a and al-Kutub al-Arba'a, in Arabic
ruling: MANUS, 27 October 2026: "lets seat the hadith" — "i mean the hadith supplementary to the quran" — "as ea-corpora". The choice of witness (OpenITI's primary versions, which name their printed editions, over a dataset that names none) and the scope (both canons and al-Nawawi's Forty) were made in session and are reported for MANUS's review.
witness_note: Rejected as witness: fawazahmed0/hadith-api (Unlicense; Arabic editions credited to 'Unknown', with no printed edition named). OpenITI's texts derive from al-Maktaba al-Shamila, the Jami' al-Kabir (JK), shiaonlinelibrary.com and the Zaydi library, as their URIs record; OpenITI reports their quality varies by source and they are not proofread against the print throughout.
